new_core_claims: OS Terrain 50 is published as grid and contour data.
The grid product uses a 50 m grid.
Grid data is supplied in ASCII grid and GML 3.2.1 formats.
Contour data is available at 10 m vertical intervals.
Contour supply includes GeoPackage.
Contour supply also includes GML, Esri shapefile and vector tiles.
ASCII grid is supplied alongside GML grid data.
Contour and grid GML use related but distinct data models.
Terrain 50 metadata follows the GEMINI standard.
Metadata distinguishes grid DTM from vector contour structure.
GML geometry uses an EPSG-based CRS identifier.
The GML model includes ContourLine features with feature identifiers.
ContourLine subtype values align with draft INSPIRE elevation concepts.
Grid and contour supplies are packaged separately by geographic tile.
A national grid supply has a documented compressed-size estimate.
GeoPackage contour layer names are defined by the specification.
Terrain 50 is intended for landscape visualisation and large-area analysis.
The data model is based on draft INSPIRE elevation concepts.
Format availability differs between grid and contour products.
Tile packaging must be resolved before claiming a TQ29 binary readback.
revalidated_core_claims: Technical specifications confirm schema and packaging, not live TQ29 bytes.
Grid spacing does not guarantee that candidate points occupy different cells.
Contour intervals cannot substitute for exact grid-cell elevations.
GML identifiers do not bind candidates without coordinate-level readback.
GEMINI metadata compliance does not prove candidate-specific measurements.
TQ29 requires direct download, byte integrity and cell extraction evidence.
Cross-source comparison requires compatible datum and coordinate handling.
Numeric promotion remains fail-closed until live TQ29 candidate-cell values are read.
